correctness.rationale: The graph uses strict endpoint interleaving to detect interior crossings; chords sharing endpoints do not cross, but identical chords are excluded separately. Independently enumerated from the alternating matching by legal re-pairings of two chords. This enumeration is complete: if the ear (0,1) is absent, their old chords are nested as (0,a),(1,b) with 1<b<a. The other chords are confined to the three intervals between 1,b,a,0; the replacement (0,1),(b,a) is noncrossing. Freeze the ear and induct on the remaining circular labels, obtaining flip connectivity to the seed. The flips only enumerate vertices; the disjoint-compatibility edges were tested separately on all unordered vertex pairs. Exact breadth-first layers from every vertex of the giant component yield 4862 vertices, 8677 edges, component sizes 1^612, 5^36 and 4070^1, all 36 order-five components stars, eccentricity histogram 10:2, 11:480, 12:483, 13:1377, 14:1368, 15:360, and exactly the specified alternating centers. The canonical graph digest agrees with both recorded outputs. This proves the finite claim only, not a formula for other sizes.

evidence: Aichholzer–Asinowski–Miltzow define the same direct adjacency. The auxiliary-object graph in arXiv:2409.03579 instead has a common disjoint-compatible spanning tree, caterpillar or path as a witness of adjacency.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Metric statements for the auxiliary graph are not equivalent to shortest paths in the direct graph. Merely naming the two rings using their degree does not identify the center.

value.rationale: k=9 is the first size with the published three-type component regime, not an arbitrary instance. The exact distance distribution supplies a transformation-length benchmark and identifies the unique optimal starting matchings in the worst case. That the uniquely highest-degree rings also minimize eccentricity does not follow from their degrees. The result is a useful exact baseline without claiming any larger-k behavior.
